# Reading in Another Language {#sec-translation}

The book is written in English, but its tools need not be used in English.

**The website edition** can be translated by your browser. In Chrome, the
[Google Translate extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/google-translate/aapbdbdomjkkjkaonfhkkikfgjllcleb)
translates the page in place (checked 2026-10-30). Code stays as written: translators skip code, so commands,
file names and the prompts in the assistant boxes remain in English. That is deliberate. The prompts name
files, columns and options that must match your project exactly, and a translated file name would no longer
be found.

**The assistant** understands many languages. You can write your own prompts in Spanish, or any other
language the model knows, and keep the literal names in backticks so they are not translated. To have the
assistant answer in Spanish while leaving code alone, make your first prompt:

::: {.prompt}
```default
Responde siempre en español; deja el código y los nombres de archivo en inglés.
```
:::

("Always reply in Spanish; leave code and file names in English.")

**The workshop's slides**, which this book follows, were designed for browser translation: their prompts are
translated for reading, while file names, columns and options are marked to stay in English
(<https://project-delphi.github.io/quarto-workshop/>).

::: practice
A translated page can mistranslate technical words. In testing, Google Translate rendered the column name
`mdm` as "señora" and "Render" as "Prestar". When a translated sentence seems odd, check the original, and
always copy literal names from the code, never from translated prose.
:::
